speakers.name: The Save Point
speakers.comment: A whole office for small lost things, and a shelf just for the singles nobody has come back for. Take a case off that shelf first. The reunions are lovely. The waiting is the part that needs somebody.

speakers.name: Deadline
speakers.comment: Mailed from eras with no post. Note that each one still arrived, and each one still has a date. Take the cancelled future. A postcard from a thing that never happened is the only one I have never been able to explain.

speakers.name: The Cartographer of Dreams
speakers.comment: A depot for the edited-out, at the end of everything. I chart what borders what, and pruned branches border nothing at all — which is the loneliest geography there is. Recover an hour rather than a person. The hour will know where it belongs.

items.title: Self-Portraits by a Thing Learning to See

speakers.name: Gary the Walrus
speakers.comment: New mind, four goes at drawing itself. Third one is usually the honest one. First is what it thinks you want, second is a correction, third is before it remembers to be embarrassed. Take the third. Same as anybody.

speakers.name: The Bookkeeper
speakers.comment: Four initialization choices, each opening a different column that will run for the life of the system. Whatever you set here becomes the first entry, and every later figure reconciles against it. Choose slowly. Nothing about a first row is small.

speakers.name: Number Two
speakers.comment: Show the henchfolk quarters. Buyers look at thrones and balconies; a lair is sold or lost on whether the staff have anywhere decent to sleep. I have stood in four of these. Only the ones with proper quarters were ever any good.

speakers.name: Vexa Thornes
speakers.comment: FOUR ROLES and an empire's edge and — and hire the one who will tell you the plan is bad. No, listen, I am being serious for a moment, which is unlike me. I filled all four with applause and I have been alone in a tower since.

items.title: Backstage at the Show That Knows You

speakers.name: The Mirror Menagerie Keeper
speakers.comment: Four doors off the wing corridor, and the ringmaster gave you the run of it, which he does not do. Shh, not you, love. Take the prop table. Whatever is going on in this tent, the props knew about it first. They always do.

items.title: The Greenhouse at the End of the World

speakers.name: Compost
speakers.comment: Never been more beautiful, and that is not irony, that is simply what a thing does at the end. We would take the overgrown control room. Something stopped managing it and it did not die. It got on with the next part.

items.title: What Grows From the Caretaker's Pockets

speakers.name: Captain Verdance
speakers.comment: The soil put those there. You did not pick them up. That distinction is the entire job, and every Caretaker I have known needed a year to accept it. Bring the smallest one into the light. The soil rarely wastes a gesture.

speakers.name: Zuzu
speakers.comment: The lamplit camp. Not the ridge, not the board. A man at a fire with nothing scheduled is the only version of me that is not somebody's business, and it lasts about an hour, and it is the one worth drawing.

speakers.name: Old Shelba
speakers.comment: Four things on the green felt and a tortoise who has outlived four generations of killers. Take the territory map. Everything else on that table is about one job. The map is about who is still standing in ten years.

speakers.name: Captain Fluke
speakers.comment: Summoned to a court at the bottom of the sea! Four currents bearing gifts! (Ship's computer notes that gifts from the deep are historically loans.) Take the one from the trench. The dark water never sends its best first.

speakers.name: Old Salt
speakers.comment: ...Not every waking is a rampage. ...Somebody finally wrote that down. ...The tiny world keeps offering things. ...Take the harbour. ...Warm water and nowhere to be. ...That is what they never draw, and it is most of what we do.

speakers.name: Detective Inspector Mochi
speakers.comment: One bulb, black velvet, four pieces laid out too neatly. Here's the thing about a fence who arranges his table: he is not selling you an object, he is selling you the order you look at them in. Start from the right.

speakers.name: The Reflection That Came Back
speakers.comment: Four slots and a half-drawn plan. Fill the last one with somebody who knows you from the inside and picked you anyway. Skills you can hire twice. That, you get offered once, and usually by somebody you nearly lost.

speakers.name: Professor Quillby
speakers.comment: A merchant of dropped things, with fibre-optic tails, offering four wares. My own doubt first, as always: I want the unrendered one, and wanting it is precisely why I should not have it. Buy the dull one. Ask what it was attached to.

speakers.name: Static
speakers.comment: Ad-rain, rooftop garden, body shop — and a dead-channel alley, folks, a DEAD CHANNEL, which is where I live. Render that one. Everybody shoots the neon. Nobody shoots the frequency nobody is watching, and it is still on.

speakers.name: Calamity
speakers.comment: A unique scenario description. Locations here. Somebody made this at two in the morning and meant to come back to it, and never did, and here it sits with a number for a name. I have been that. It ain't nothing. It's just early.

speakers.name: Nix Farrow
speakers.comment: She came up a night EARLY. Nobody's ready, half the sellers are still out past the breakers, and Corvid's broadcast is a day behind its own truth. I've got that in the book. I did not write it in. It was already there.

speakers.name: Whisk Tallow
speakers.comment: A debt owed by the market itself, and the kid wants a second pair of eyes on it. Good instinct. That entry is in my hand and I did not put it there, and I have checked twice, and I would rather somebody else read it aloud.

speakers.name: Tinny
speakers.comment: A laugh that hisses back open every time. I know that sound from the inside — that is not a bad seal, friend, that is a sound with somewhere left to go. The Choir won't sing the old echo because the old echo is the rest of it.

speakers.name: Gaia
speakers.comment: He listened to something that was not his, and now he must choose between delivering it plain or arriving with an explanation. Small one, they are the same round. Take the words. The doorstep is easier when somebody stands on it a moment longer.

speakers.name: Undersecretary Wrenna Vail
speakers.comment: They wish to borrow against collateral that is not theirs, because a fragment adhered to them on the stair and they cannot prove it. I keep everything and I have nothing of my own on those shelves. I am not the right person to refuse this.
